frase_gancho.texto: The city where, according to the Mexica, men become gods.

introduccion_narrativa.texto: From Cuicuilco, which fell beneath the lava, we move on to the city that rose. When the Mexica reached these ruins, Teotihuacán had been abandoned for centuries, and it seemed so enormous to them that they believed only the gods could have built it. That is why they called it “the place where men become gods.” At its height, around the year four hundred fifty of our era, it had streets laid out in a grid, temples painted red, and neighborhoods of artisans, with more than one hundred thousand inhabitants according to many estimates. Here you will find a façade of serpents, a stone goddess weighing several tons, a painted paradise, an old man who carries fire, and the faces with which they bade farewell to their dead.
